text:
sarah: Noticed a spike in tiny-gpu pod requeues in us-west2 ~02:05 UTC. App teams seeing transient 502/503. Can we investigate?

vincent: I pulled scheduler traces. There's a relabel sweep that toggled gpu-arch labels on ~30 nodes between 02:03-02:06. Many pods with nodeAffinity to gpu-arch=ampere were bounced because the label flip made them ineligible, scheduler preempted then kept failing to bind.

deepa: Also saw kube-proxy restarts on a subset of nodes — conntrack saturations around same time. That magnified the problem because pods couldn't connect to the API server during rebind attempts.

ops-bot: [alert] evictions.spike(us-west2) 7799991234 - 62 evictions in 12m, reschedule-failures 18, api-errors 9

vincent: Example scheduler log excerpt:
```
E0324 02:04:12 scheduler_extender.go:120] preempting pod model-worker-17 due to label-mismatch: node gpu-arch changed
E0324 02:04:13 binder.go:198] bind failed: node affinity conflict: required gpu-arch=ampere, node has gpu-arch=unknown
E0324 02:04:14 evictor.go:76] eviction succeeded, requeueing pod, attempt=2
```

deepa: The relabel job was the automated "reconcile-gpu-families" cron that runs nightly. It uses a rolling replace and temporarily sets gpu-arch=unknown when toggling. That's the root cause.

sarah: Oof. We need a two-part response: immediate mitigation to stop further churn and a durable change to the relabel flow.

vincent: Short term I can:
- pause the relabel cron in us-west2 (kubectl patch cronjob)
- scale up warm-pool for tiny-gpu by +3 replicas in us-west2 to absorb pending pods
- add a scheduler guard: --label-stability-window=120s so nodes with recent label mutation are treated as unstable and not considered for preemption-based relocation

deepa: I'm in favor of the label-stability-window flag. Also, bump conntrack max to reduce kube-proxy restarts while we stabilize: ssh to nodes & sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144 (or via daemonset).

ops-bot: [note] action scheduled: pause cron reconcile-gpu-families in us-west2 at 7799991300 by sarah

vincent: Command I used to pause cron (can rollback):
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch cronjob reconcile-gpu-families --type merge -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
```

sarah: Cost/impact estimate for the window: ~30 minutes of churn, ~3.1 GPU-hours wasted, rough cost hit +14% for the hour. We should include that in postmortem.

deepa: Medium-term fixes I propose:
- change relabeler to use a two-phase tag: set gpu-arch=staging-ampere first, run verification probes, then flip gpu-arch=ampere. Avoid setting an unknown/empty label.
- add post-relabel quiesce period (default 2m) before any drain/preempt operations kick in
- instrument "label-mutation-rate" metric and alert if >5 nodes in 1m
- default tiny-gpu workload class to disallow fractional-gang until warm-pool autoscaling is tuned

vincent: One more safety: when relabeler runs, create a maintenance annotation on nodes so the scheduler can treat them as maintenance and skip preemptive evictions: node.kubernetes.io/maintenance=true. That avoids preemptive churn.

sarah: Agreed. Let's prioritize: 1) Pause cron and bump warm-pool+conntrack (now) 2) Roll in label-stability-window to canary (us-west2-a) 3) Implement two-phase relabeler + quiesce in next sprint.

ops-bot: [resolve] evictions.spike mitigated in us-west2-a after action 7799991300; watch window 30m

deepa: Canary notes: after pausing cron and adding two warm nodes, eviction rate dropped to baseline in us-west2-a; still watching conntrack tail in us-west2-b.

vincent: Opening follow-up issues: ENG-PLAT-4721 (relabeler two-phase + quiesce), ENG-PLAT-4722 (scheduler label-stability feature), ENG-PLAT-4723 (conntrack daemonset tuning). I'll link cost numbers.

sarah: Thanks team. Please add runbook section "Relabeler-induced affinity churn" with rollback steps and the kubectl pause command. I'll write the short postmortem after 24h of observation. :memo:
